title: Chat log scraper as structured session ground truth
summary: Scrape the Foundry chat log to extract inline-check results in structured form (who rolled, against what DC, what degree of success) so a session's actual events become queryable data rather than living only in scrollback.
description: A scraper that reads Foundry's chat log and pulls out inline-check results in structured form — who tried, what they tried against, what degree of success they got. The stated goal: build up a total, durable set of knowledge about the adventure as actually played, not as planned. This is the mechanism that would make dialogue-management-panel's recorded outcomes (and any other inline @Check result) queryable after the session ends. Explicitly framed as feeding, alongside player-and-gm-journals-context-ingestion, into how future episodes get written — a complete before/after picture of a session: what the GM improvised, what actually happened mechanically, and what players privately thought about it.
sourceContext: User planning message on dialogue/journal/campaign-management systems, prior to the ideas/ system existing — originally captured as prose in design/campaign-arc.md's 'Foundry module: new concept threads' section, migrated here on audit.
openSubQuestions: Exact data shape for a scraped check result.
Where this data lives (a flag-based store per the harvest mechanism already designed, or something else).
How 'who tried what' maps back to the labeled subjects in dialogue-management-panel specifically vs. general combat/skill rolls.
